raw_segments.text: Emilia, yes, a dozen, and as many to the vantage as would store the world they played for.
But I do think it is their husbands' faults if wives do fall, say that they slack their
duties and pour our treasures into foreign laps, or else break out in peevish jealousies
throwing restraint upon us, or say they strike us or scant our former having in despite.
Why, we have Gauls, and though we have some grace, yet have we some revenge.
Let husbands know their wives have sense like them. They see and smell and have their
palates both for sweet and sour as husbands have. What is it that they do when they change
us for others? Is it sport? I think it is. And doth affection breed it? I think it doth.
Ist frailty that thus errs. It is so too. And have not we affections, desires for sport,
and frailty as men have. Then let them use us well, else let them know, the ills we do,
